content.text: ▪︎⍉known cause - may be assoc w HHV-6
▪︎IBD · celiac dz · SLE · B12/folate deficiency · HIV · MTX
▪︎also assoc: genetic predisposition · IS · poor oral hygiene · food allergies + stress
▪︎simple aphthosis = MC form - sporadic episodes throughout the yr, limited to oral mucosa - ulcers typically 3-5 mm + heal w.in 1-2 wks
▪︎complex aphthosis = oral + genital mucosa ulcers - typically >1 cm · more painful than simple + can take up to 6 wks to heal - USU ≥1 active ulcer
▪︎ulcer morphology: minor · major or herpetiform - herpetiform = 1-2 mm each in clusters - may coalesce into lrger ulcers
▪︎recurr oral + genital ulcers → evaluate for Behçet syndrome
▪︎often triggered by minimal trauma (ex, biting tongue)
▪︎appear on nonkeratinized mucosa (buccal + lip mucosa) - rarely labia minora (Lipschütz ulcer)
▪︎pain mgmt: 2% viscous lidocaine · diphenhydramine liquid or dyclonine lozenges
▪︎2ndry infect w Candida or bacteria → clotrimazole troches · nystatin suspensions or chlorhexidine mouth rinses
▪︎dexamethasone elixir = 1st-line for simple stomatitis - most effective if started @ sx onset
▪︎complex stomatitis unresponsive to topical therapies → PO prednisone x4-7 days
▪︎⍉single effective tx - goals: maintain good oral hygiene · ⍉exacerbating factors + ↓pain
▪︎soft bristle toothbrush + gently floss daily to ⍉↑trauma - wax over abrasive points of braces
▪︎nonalcohol mouthwash - ⍉sodium lauryl sulfate-containing toothpaste - ⍉foods that seem to exacerbate sx
: S. viridans · H. influenzae · S. pneumoniae · S. pyogenes
: obstruct (ex, stones) · dehydration · immune dx · advanced age · malnutrition
▪︎↑risk: older postop pts · poor oral hygiene · prematurity/↓birth wt
acute onset unilat · painful swelling & erythema overlying salivary gland
▪︎firm swelling from preauricular area to angle of mandible (d/c from Stensen duct)
▪︎d/c from Stensen duct: gram stain + cx
▪︎admit for hydration + IV abx - infect can spread to deep fascial spaces (life-threatening)
▪︎empiric regimen var: community- vs hsp-acquired (often hsp-acquired in older postop pts)
▪︎community-acquired: amp-sulbactam OR cefuroxime + metronidazole - nafcillin + (ceftriaxone or levofloxacin) or + (metronidazole or clindamycin)
▪︎hsp-acquired/IC: (vanco or linezolid) + cefepime + metronidazole · imipenem · meropenem or pip-tazo
▪︎outpt PO options: amox-clav OR clindamycin OR cephalosporin + metronidazole
▪︎comp: spread to deep fascial spaces (life-threatening) · resp obstruct · septic thrombophlebitis (Lemierre) · bacteremia · osteomyelitis
▪︎noninfectious: sialolithiasis · ETOH use d/o · DM · uremia · drugs (anticholinergics, antihist) · malig
bilat parotid gland swelling w.o purulent d/c
▪︎HSV lesions: burning sensation → painful vesicles break open + crust over
▪︎herpes lesions MC on outside of mouth (vs aphthous ulcers: oral mucosa)
▪︎counsel pts to ⍉oral sex until lesions completely resolve
▪︎triggers: stress · menstruation · UV sunlight · fever · lip trauma
▪︎prophylactic acyclovir or valacyclovir if ≥6 HSV outbreaks/yr
